title: Scalable and Asynchronous Differential Checkpointing for Intermittently Powered Devices
problem: Intermittently powered devices relying on checkpoint-recovery face scalability challenges: hardware-based differential checkpointing costs increase proportionally with memory size, and synchronous checkpointing blocks the MCU during backups, causing unacceptable latency.
motivation: Batteryless energy harvesting systems require efficient checkpointing to survive frequent power failures, but current approaches don't scale to devices with increasing memory capacity or support non-blocking checkpoint operations.
method: FLASC is a hardware-software co-design enabling scalable and asynchronous differential checkpointing. The approach: (1) uses memory modification tracking that scales with increasing memory size; (2) supports safe asynchronous checkpoint execution allowing MCU to continue work during backups; (3) combines efficient synchronization mechanisms with reduced hardware overhead through smart software-hardware partitioning.
key_novelty: Hardware-software co-designed differential checkpointing achieving scalability and asynchronous operation without proportional hardware cost growth.
contributions: Scalable memory modification tracking mechanism that avoids hardware cost proportional to memory size
Support for safe asynchronous checkpoint execution enabling MCU progress during backups
9.4% faster execution compared to state-of-the-art while using only 49.1% hardware resources
6.9× better scalability with increasing data memory size addressing prior architectural limitations

metrics.other: 6.9× better scalability with memory size; 1.85× efficiency per hardware resource

limitations: Evaluation limited to FPGA prototyping; silicon implementation and applicability to very large memory systems (>1GB) is not demonstrated.
primary_theme: Scalable asynchronous checkpointing for intermittent devices
